title: Natural selection removes forms rather than originating them

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Natural selection removes forms rather than originating them

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Since forms, including exaggerated ones such as the great Secondary reptiles and Tertiary mammals, can arise from changes in growth, natural selection is needed to explain their disappearance rather than their appearance; in general its function is not to originate but to remove.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. III: The Rate of Growth

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And we then, I think, draw near to the conclusion that what is true of these is universally true, and that the great function of natural selection is not to originate, but to remove

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter III, “The Rate of Growth”; topic “Growth stimulants and natural selection”. Scope: evolution of organic form generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch03-29: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.40

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A restricted temporal prediction can be tested, but Thompson's universal division of causal roles is underspecified and difficult to distinguish from standard views in which selection changes variant frequencies. Existing macroevolutionary data address examples, not the universal assertion.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define origination as the appearance of phenotypic variants through developmental change and removal as differential extinction or reproductive loss, then compare the timing of variation with subsequent selection in fossil and population time series. Evidence that variants predate selective sorting supports the restricted proposition, while the universal claim would require this sequence across evolutionary transitions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fossil sampling obscures the timing and causes of appearance and disappearance.

Origination and removal are partly conceptual categories.

Universal scope cannot be established from available cases.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.3

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The sentence is a claim about the proper role of selection, not a statement with a distinct measurable consequence. Any pattern of exaggerated forms arising and later vanishing can be read either as Thompson reads it or as selection among growth variants. Existing fossil inventories therefore cannot settle it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The wording assigns natural selection a function, removal rather than origination. Fossil appearances and extinctions of large reptiles and mammals do not supply a variable that would count as origination-by-selection in one outcome and origination-by-growth in another.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Growth-rate change and selection on growth-rate variants predict the same fossil shapes.

Stratigraphic appearance and disappearance are compatible with selection both producing and culling variants.

operationalizability: 0.2
